subject.title: Bug: Built-in dreaming system contaminates agent identity in multi-agent setups

question: Should memory-core dreaming enforce agent isolation as a hard boundary for shared workspaces, and should the active path be the allowlist PR or a narrower agent-scoped corpus/recall fix?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and security-relevant, but the open PR adds public config/API surface and appears only partially overlapping with the shared-workspace identity boundary.

options.title: Enforce Hard Agent Isolation
options.body: Keep this issue open and land or replace the fix so shared-workspace dreaming cannot read, rank, narrate, or promote another agent's sessions by default.

options.title: Accept Workspace Pooling With Docs
options.body: Declare workspace-level dreaming pooling expected behavior and update multi-agent docs and security guidance to make that explicit.

options.title: Fold Into Broader Memory Isolation
options.body: Pause a narrow fix and coordinate this with the broader multi-agent memory/privacy isolation work, accepting that the dreaming-specific bug remains open longer.

recommendation.title: Enforce Hard Agent Isolation
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and land or replace the fix so shared-workspace dreaming cannot read, rank, narrate, or promote another agent's sessions by default.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned on the live issue and already narrowed the bug to the shared-workspace isolation decision.
